title: History's Plot Twists
blurb: Empires, explorers and inventors did weirder stuff than any movie. One per card is cap.

cards.say: [Vikings were cutting wood in Newfoundland in the year 1021], [Marco Polo brought noodles home to Italy from China in 1295], [Ibn Battuta traveled about 75,000 miles in the 1300s], and [Zheng He's Chinese fleet reached East Africa in the 1410s].
cards.real: Italians were already eating pasta before Marco Polo got home in 1295. The noodle story came from a 1929 pasta trade magazine.

cards.say: [Thomas Edison's very first patent was for an electric vote counter], [a dentist helped invent the cotton candy machine], [Louis Braille created his reading system for blind people at age 15], and [Benjamin Franklin got rich from the patents on his inventions].
cards.real: Franklin never patented any of his inventions. He wrote that since we all gain from other people's inventions, we should share ours freely.

cards.say: [Julius Caesar was the very first Roman emperor], [ancient Romans grabbed fast food at street-side counters], [ancient Greeks built a gear-driven machine that predicted eclipses], and [the Romans had a goddess who looked after the sewers].
cards.real: Caesar ruled Rome as dictator but was never emperor. His adopted heir Augustus became Rome's first emperor in 27 BC.

cards.say: [the Inca built over 20,000 miles of roads without using the wheel], [Mansa Musa spent so much gold in Cairo in 1324 that its value dropped], [the Mongol Empire conquered Japan in the 1280s], and [the Ottoman Empire lasted more than 600 years].
cards.real: The Mongols tried to invade Japan in 1274 and again in 1281. Both attacks failed, partly because of huge storms.

cards.say: [the first animals ever sent into space were two monkeys], [the Apollo 11 crew filled out a customs form after coming home], [astronaut Alan Shepard hit golf balls on the Moon], and [Buzz Aldrin snapped a selfie during a spacewalk in 1966].
cards.real: The first animals in space were fruit flies, launched on a US rocket in 1947. Monkeys came later.

cards.say: [the stolen 1966 World Cup trophy was found by a dog named Pickles], [the Mona Lisa was stolen in 1911 and not found again until 1925], [the Statue of Liberty worked as a lighthouse for 16 years], and [a real moth got stuck inside a Harvard computer in 1947].
cards.real: The Mona Lisa was stolen from the Louvre in 1911 and turned up in Italy in December 1913, about two years later.

cards.say: [Abraham Lincoln is in the National Wrestling Hall of Fame], [Ben Franklin invented swim fins when he was a kid], [Queen Elizabeth II trained as a mechanic during World War II], and [George Washington's false teeth were carved out of wood].
cards.real: Washington's dentures were made of ivory, metal, and human and animal teeth. None of them were wood.

cards.say: [bubble wrap was first invented to be a textured wallpaper], [the Slinky was invented by a naval engineer working with springs], [a melted candy bar led to the invention of the microwave oven], and [Velcro was inspired by the sticky feet of geckos].
cards.real: Velcro was inspired by burrs that stuck to an engineer's dog after a walk in the Swiss countryside in 1941.

cards.say: [the Eiffel Tower escaped being torn down because it was useful for radio], [the Leaning Tower of Pisa started leaning before it was finished], [King Tut's tomb was found empty, cleaned out by ancient robbers], and [Machu Picchu was built for an Inca emperor around 1450].
cards.real: Robbers did break in twice long ago, but the tomb was found mostly intact in 1922, with more than 5,000 objects inside.

cards.say: [winners at the first modern Olympics in 1896 got gold medals], [tug-of-war was an Olympic sport until 1920], [painters and sculptors won Olympic medals until 1948], and [the first basketball game, in 1891, used peach baskets and a soccer ball].
cards.real: In 1896, winners got a silver medal and an olive branch. Gold medals for first place started in 1904.

cards.say: [Lewis and Clark brought a Newfoundland dog named Seaman on their trip], [Columbus sailed west to prove that the Earth was round], [America was named after explorer Amerigo Vespucci on a 1507 map], and [Magellan's crew left Spain with five ships and came back with one].
cards.real: Educated Europeans already knew the Earth was round. Columbus's argument was about its size, which he guessed far too small.

cards.say: [the first known photo of a person shows a man getting his boots shined], [the first traffic light, put up in London in 1868, ran on gas], [Alexander Graham Bell's first phone call was to his mother], and [the first person charged with speeding was going 8 miles per hour].
cards.real: Bell's first call, in 1876, was to his assistant Thomas Watson in the next room, asking him to come over.
